title: Scatter-gather KV page-cache prefetch patterns and microkernel notes
content:
Purpose
-----
Notes and experimental ideas for a scatter-gather style prefetcher that plays nicely with paged KV and fused attention kernels. Goal: reduce long-tail token latency when serving variable-length chat workloads, minimize extra memory traffic, and avoid stalling FlashAttention-style microkernels under paged KV misses. This is an exploratory doc — lots of heuristics and TODOs.

Background / problem statement
----------------------------
- In paged KV setups we keep active KV pages on device and evict cold pages to host or NVMe. Requests for long contexts can cause unpredictable host round-trips.
- Standard prefetch schemes (prefetch entire page on first access) can be overfetching for workloads that touch narrow token ranges across many sequences (e.g., multi-user streaming).
- FlashAttention and fused attention kernels are sensitive to kernel-entry jitter: a single request that blocks on host fetch can stall queues and increase scheduling jitter for other warps on the same SM.

Design hypothesis
-----------------
1) Use a cooperative scatter-gather prefetch that only pulls the subpage ranges required by in-flight KV accesses rather than full pages.
2) Combine prefetch hints injected by the runtime with lightweight on-device token access tracing to adapt future prefetches.
3) Add a non-blocking fallback path for attention microkernels: if KV slot is missing, run a reduced-latency approximate attention that uses local cache + compact fallback embedding until host fetch completes, then resync.

Key constraints
---------------
- Prefetch cost must be lower than the added latency from misses across realistic request mixes.
- GPU occupancy should not be starved by heavyweight host->device memory copies. Avoid launching big DMA operations in kernel-critical paths.
- Prefetch strategy must behave nicely with batching and request coalescing: if multiple requests map to the same page range, coalesce fetches.

Architecture sketch
------------------
1) Request arrives at runtime. Route selects model shard and target device.
2) For each request, compute the expected KV indices to be accessed for the next N tokens (N=window horizon, initially 8). This uses sequence-length distribution + tokenizer heuristics.
3) Translate indices to page(s) + subpage ranges. Emit prefetch hints to a per-GPU prefetch queue. Hints include: page_id, byte_range, priority, deadline_ts, correlation_id (for coalescing).
4) Prefetch worker (host thread + small on-device command stream) coalesces hints and issues async host->device copies.
5) On kernel entry, the microkernel checks a compact in-GPU bloom/bitmap of resident subranges. If missing, kernel uses NOP-fast fallback for only those tokens (see fallback below) and places a guarantee marker with correlation_id to trigger urgent prefetch.

Prefetch worker heuristics
------------------------
- Coalesce window: group hints targeting adjacent byte ranges within 4KB of each other.
- Priority: requests near tail of an active chat get higher priority. Background batches lower priority and can be throttled.
- Deadline scheduling: compute cost of miss = estimated kernel stall + probability of subsequent hits; prioritize hints with highest expected benefit per byte.
- Rate-limit host->device submission to avoid hogging PCIe/GPUDirect. Use token-bucket keyed by device and model-shard.

In-GPU metadata structures
-------------------------
- Resident-subrange bitmap: one bit per 256B subrange of a page. Small and fast to query in kernel. Pack into 64-bit words and align for warp-friendly checks.
- Correlation table (LRU limited): maps correlation_id -> pending hint meta (useful for cancellation and debugging). Kept on host but mirrored small version on GPU for fast checks (stale allowed).

Kernel-level check + fallback sequence
-------------------------------------
Pseudocode (simplified):

// inside fused-attn kernel before reading KV slot
int subrange_idx = compute_subrange(kv_offset);
if (!resident_bitmap.test(subrange_idx)) {
  // fast path: do light-weight local fallback for this token
  apply_approximate_attention_for_token(); // e.g., shrink key dims, reuse small cache
  // push hint into on-device hint queue (lock-free)
  push_device_hint(correlation_id, subrange_idx);
} else {
  load_kv_from_device();
}

Notes on fallback: keep it cheap. Examples:
- Use 8-bit quantized keys stored on-chip for last-K tokens (tiny circular buffer).
- Use attention over compressed keys (projected keys to much smaller dim) to produce approximate output until full KV arrives.
- Error injection experiments: measure divergence and decide thresholds for when approximate outputs are acceptable.

Coalescing and dynamic stride tuning
-----------------------------------
- Track access patterns per model shard: sequential vs. scatter. Maintain a simple exponential moving average (EMA) of stride lengths and scatter density.
- If stride < threshold -> prefetch contiguous ranges aggressively. If scatter density high -> prefer tiny subrange pulls and increase coalescing window to avoid repeated host trips.

Microbench experiments (notes and partial results)
------------------------------------------------
Testbed: A100-40G, NVMe-backed host pages, synthetic replay traces from 3 customer workloads (multi-chat, long-form doc, bursty search). Measurements are rough early runs.
- Baseline (full-page on first access): mean latency p50=18ms, p95=73ms, p99=210ms
- Simple subrange prefetch (256B granularity), no coalescing: p50=17ms, p95=58ms, p99=140ms (reduced p99 but more PCIe ops)
- Cooperative prefetch with coalescing + rate limit: p50=16.8ms, p95=52ms, p99=98ms (best tradeoff in these traces)
- Fallback mode enabled (approx-attn): p95 improved by ~12%, p99 improved by 30% in mixed workloads; small loss in output quality for the long-doc traces (measured by perplexity increase ~0.6%)

Open questions + risks
---------------------
- How to bound memory fragmentation on-device when pulling many small subranges? Need a compact allocator and slab policy keyed by model-shard.
- Security: ensure prefetch hints don't leak cross-tenant access patterns; add tenant-aware isolation for prefetch metadata.
- Complexity: more moving parts increases surface for bugs during canary rollouts.
- Determinism: approximate fallback produces nondeterministic outputs that complicate eval runs; need guardrails to only enable on latency SLOs.

TODO / next experiments
----------------------
- Implement device-side resident bitmap + lock-free hint queue prototype (Jon) - ticket SRV-847.
- Run longer A/B on live traffic in staging with fallback off-by-default; collect divergence metrics (Sofia).
- Try alternate subrange sizes (64B, 512B) and record PCIe ops vs. latency curves (Aamir).
- Integrate with existing rollout infrastructure: rollouts should support traffic split by tenant and fallback gating.

Notes to self / misc
-------------------
- See GH PR 1427 for the device hint queue sketch.
- Slack thread: some concerns from infra about extra host threads for coalescing; consider piggybacking on existing DMA workers.
- We should instrument per-model shard: PCIe bytes pulled, number of subrange fetches, coalesce ratio, fallback rate.

Appendix: quick ascii of memory layout
------------------------------------
PAGE (64KB)
|---- slab0 (hot) ----|---- slab1 ----|---- slab2 ----|---- free ----|
subrange idx: 0..255 (256 subranges at 256B) -> resident_bitmap length 256 bits -> 4 x 64-bit words.

End of notes.
